body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not always provide a minimum 12-month eligibility period for each child, as required by 98.21(a)(1). (Plan Question 2.5.2a) • The Lead Agency's policy for discontinuing assistance for excessive unexplained absences does not include multiple attempts to contact the family and provider, as required by 98.21(a)(5)(i)(A). (Plan Question 2.5.3cii) Overall Target Completion Date: 05/31/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead Agency does not always provide a minimum 12-month eligibility period for each child, as required by 98.21(a)(1). (Plan Question 2.5.2a) 05/31/2026 2 The Lead Agency will revise Title 392 regulations. 01/31/2025 3 The Lead Agency will work with the state’s eligibility systems to make changes that will allow for a 12-month eligibility period for each child. 03/31/2025 4 Training and guidance documents will be updated. Lead Agency staff will receive training on the new process. 04/30/2026 5 12-month eligibility will be fully implemented. 05/31/2026 6 The Lead Agency's policy for discontinuing assistance for excessive unexplained absences does not include multiple attempts to contact the family and provider, as required by 98.21(a)(5)(i)(A). (Plan Question 2.5.3cii) 05/31/2026 7 Lead Agency staff will be trained to make three attempts to contact families if a provider reports the child has unexplained absences for more than three consecutive days. Lead Agency staff training will be updated, and a memo to Lead Agency staff will be sent. 04/30/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency standard for emergency preparedness and response planning does not include staff training for licensed family child care homes, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vii). (Plan Question 5.3.7v) • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on emergency preparedness and response planning for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, or license-exempt family child care homes, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1g) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed family child care providers for compliance with a standard for emergency preparedness and response planning, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). Additionally, the Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers and licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to emergency preparedness and response planning, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 09/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead Agency standard for emergency preparedness and response planning does not include staff training for licensed family child care homes, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vii). (Plan Question 5.3.7v) 09/30/2025 2 The Lead Agency will revise the Prepare to Care and Lincoln/Lancaster Health and Safety trainings to include appropriate CCDF information. 09/30/2025 3 The Lead Agency will require all child care staff in all facility types to complete emergency preparedness and response planning. 09/30/2025 4 The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed family child care providers for compliance with a standard for emergency preparedness and response planning, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B). Additionally, the Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers and licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license-exempt family child care 09/30/2025 providers for compliance with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to emergency preparedness and response planning, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) 5 Lead Agency staff will be trained to monitor trainings completed by child care staff. 09/30/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR for substitutes in licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, or license-exempt family child care, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1m) • The Lead Agency annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care providers, and annual inspection for license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR does not cover substitutes, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 05/31/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR for substitutes in licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, or license- exempt family child care, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1m) 05/31/2025 2 The Lead Agency will update the definition of staff in Title 392 regulations to include substitutes. 01/31/2025 3 The Lead Agency will add the definition of staff to the child care enrollment agreement. The Lead Agency will require child care staff to complete pediatric first aid and CPR. 05/31/2025 4 The Lead Agency annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care providers, and annual inspection for license- exempt family child care providers for compliance 05/31/2025 with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR does not cover substitutes, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) 5 Train Lead Agency staff to monitor trainings completed by child care staff/substitutes. 05/31/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a group size for toddlers, preschoolers, school- age children, or mixed age groups in licensed centers, as required by 98.41(d)(1). body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a standard for the prevention of shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma for licensed centers, licensed family child care, license-exempt family child care, or for prevention of child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care, license-exempt family child care, and out-of-school providers, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vi). (Plan Questions 5.3.6ai, 5.3.6aii, 5.3.6av, 5.3.6avii, 5.3.6bi, 5.3.6bii, 5.3.6bv, and 5.3.6bvii) • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on prevention of shaken baby syndrome, abusive head trauma, and child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, and license-exempt family child care, or on child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, license- exempt family child care, and out-of-school providers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1f) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care, or an annual inspection for license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for the prevention of shaken baby syndrome, abusive head trauma, and child maltreatment and with related pre-service or orientation training requirements, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 09/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead Agency has not established a standard for the prevention of shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma for licensed centers, licensed family child care, license-exempt family child care, or for prevention of child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care, license-exempt family child care, and out-of- school providers, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vi). (Plan Questions 5.3.6ai, 5.3.6aii, 5.3.6av, 5.3.6avii, 5.3.6bi, 5.3.6bii, 5.3.6bv, and 5.3.6bvii) 09/30/2025 2 The Lead Agency will create a standard for the prevention of shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma. 03/31/2025 3 The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on prevention of shaken baby syndrome, abusive head trauma, and child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, and license-exempt family child care, or on child maltreatment for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, license- exempt family child care, and out-of-school providers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1f) 09/30/2025 4 The Lead Agency will revise the Prepare to Care and Lincoln/Lancaster Health and Safety trainings to include appropriate CCDF information. 09/30/2025 5 The Lead Agency will add the standard to the Subsidy Guidance Document. 09/30/2025 6 The Lead Agency will add the standard to the child care enrollment agreement. The Lead Agency will require all child care staff to complete Prepare to Care. 09/30/2025 7 The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or 09/30/2025 licensed family child care, or an annual inspection for license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for the prevention of shaken baby syndrome, abusive head trauma, and child maltreatment and with related pre- service or orientation training requirements, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, and 5.5.2bi) 8 Train Lead Agency staff to monitor trainings completed by child care staff related to the identification and reporting of child abuse. 09/30/2025
